subject: Region binding, decommission window and snapshot deletion Q&A
messages:
From: Alice Bryant <alice.bryant@finsecure.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: compliance@finsecure.com
Date: 2026-12-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Clarify region pinning and snapshot deletion cadence for Dedicated environment

Jonas —

Thanks for taking this on. As we scope Redwood Dedicated for our production workloads, the procurement & security teams have a handful of practical questions we need answered before we sign off:

1) Region pinning: can you confirm the exact granularity of "pinning"? Is it region-level (e.g., us-west-2) or AZ-level? Do backups/snapshots ever cross the pinned region for replication or DR?

2) Snapshot retention and deletion: when a tenant is decommissioned we need evidence that all snapshots and replicas are destroyed. What does the deletion workflow look like (who triggers it, what systems perform the wipe, SLA for irrevocable deletion)? We also need an artifact we can keep in our audit file that shows deletion occurred (timestamped log entry or signed handoff).

3) Restore window and rollback: if you destroy snapshots as part of a decommission, is there a short hang/soft-retention window for emergency restore? If so, how long and how is access gated?

4) Cross-region fallbacks: if you failover traffic, what assurances exist that data is not copied outside the pinned boundary or retained beyond the retention window?

If you can provide a short runbook excerpt and an estimated timeline for the deletion evidence and a contact for a follow-up call next week, that will help unblock our legal & procurement teams.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we are targeting a go/no-go with our security committee on 2026-12-27.

Best,
Alice Bryant
Head of Cloud Security, FinSecure Inc.
compliance@finsecure.com

Attachments: none listed
From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Bryant <alice.bryant@finsecure.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-18T13:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify region pinning and snapshot deletion cadence for Dedicated environment

Alice — thanks for the clear list. I summarized below and attached a short diagram + SLA table to make this consumable for procurement. Quick answers up front, with a compact mutual action plan at the end.

Short answers:
- Pinning granularity: region-level (AWS region; e.g., us-west-2). We do not pin at AZ level.
- Replication: snapshots and primary live data are constrained to the pinned region for Dedicated clusters. Cross-region replication only occurs for explicit DR contracts and only after customer opt-in; otherwise, no cross-region copies are made.
- Deletion workflow: decommission is initiated by the customer's org admin (or Redwood SRE on request). The pipeline: mark tenant -> evict processes -> snapshot finalization -> snapshot deletion job (idempotent) -> metadata tombstone -> scrub ephemeral caches -> verify via audit-run logs. Irrevocable deletion SLA is 72 hours after the deletion job is executed; we provide a timestamped audit entry and signed attestation on request.
- Emergency restore window: by default we do not keep a soft-retention beyond the deletion SLA. For a short grace period (configurable) we can enable a 14-day soft-retention; access is gated to a named set of SRE roles and requires signed approval from the customer's security contact.

What I'm attaching:
- redwood-dedicated-dataflow-diagram.pdf (mapping of live, snapshot, and ephemeral cache flows)
- pinning-sla-table.csv (SLA and timelines for deletion vs. optional grace window)

Mutual action items (proposed):
1) By 2026-12-21: FinSecure to confirm whether you need the 14-day emergency soft-retention or opt for standard immediate deletion (72h irrevocable).
2) By 2026-12-22: Redwood to provide a runbook excerpt + deletion attestation template (attached as an excerpt).
3) 2026-12-23: 30-minute sync (SRE + Compliance) to walk the audit artifact and access gating. Please propose slots.

If OK I'll also loop in Product Compliance (Soojin) to ensure the attestation template meets your auditable evidence needs.

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-dataflow-diagram.pdf, pinning-sla-table.csv

Date: 2026-12-19T08:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify region pinning and snapshot deletion cadence for Dedicated environment

Thanks Jonas — that helps a lot. A couple quick follow-ups before our security committee review:

- For the 72-hour irrevocable deletion SLA, what exactly is included in the timestamped audit entry (log fields)? We need at least: tenant id, deletion job id, initiating principal, list of affected snapshot ids, and a SHA256 of snapshot manifest. Can you confirm you can provide those fields?

- For the optional 14-day soft-retention, please confirm the approval workflow: we require (1) ticket created in our JIRA with approval from FinSecure Security lead; (2) Redwood SRE to mark request and provide email-based confirmation; (3) automatic expiry after 14 days with the same deletion pipeline executed.

- Regarding backups: do cold backups (for long-term archival) ever leave the pinned region? If a customer purchases archival storage, we need explicit confirmation whether archival copies are kept inside the region or may be moved to a secondary region for cost optimization.

If you can confirm the exact log fields and the archival behavior we should be able to give you a yes/no on the soft-retention today. I can join a call on 2026-12-23 afternoon PT if that helps.

Best,
Alice

Subject: Re: Clarify region pinning and snapshot deletion cadence for Dedicated environment

Alice / team — quick confirmation from operations and the attestation we will provide.

1) Audit log fields: yes — the deletion attestation will include: tenant_id, deletion_job_id, initiating_principal (email + Redwood SSO id), list_of_snapshot_ids, snapshot_manifest_sha256, deletion_timestamp_utc, and runbook_version. We will sign the attestation with our compliance PGP key and provide the signed artifact as a PDF that you can store in your audit file.

2) Archival/cold backups: archival storage is an opt-in add-on. If elected, archival copies are kept inside the pinned region by default. We will only move archival objects outside the region for explicit cost-tiering agreements and only with customer approval documented in a signed addendum.

3) Soft-retention workflow: we confirm your three-step workflow is acceptable (create JIRA ticket + customer security approval + Redwood SRE mark). Redwood will enforce an automatic expiry that triggers the identical deletion pipeline; the expiry run will emit the same signed attestation.

Next steps:
- I uploaded a runbook excerpt and the attestation template to the Drive link shared above.
- If you want the soft-retention enabled for the first migration, reply with approval and the JIRA key; we'll flip the flag and provide the first attestations post-decommission.

If it helps, I can join the 12/23 afternoon PT sync alongside Jonas and Soojin.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Head of Dedicated Ops, Redwood Inference
